brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Auction House" where users bid on fragments of their own forgotten memories, represented as partially obscured polaroid photographs that gradually reveal themselves b

dominant_strengths: Conceptually evocative circular seance arrangement of polaroids creates ritualistic auction-table metaphor that suits the memory bidding premise
Restrained warm-on-black palette with subtle teardrop currency icons (joy/sorrow/nostalgia) hints at poetic resource system
dominant_weaknesses: Polaroids are entirely blank with no fragment imagery, captions, bid state, or timer—the core auction interaction is invisible
No bidding affordances, hierarchy, or active focus; six identical cards read as decorative rather than interactive lots
Typography is generic sans-serif at one weight, missing the literary/archival voice the concept demands
fix_priorities: Add per-polaroid metadata: blurred preview, current bid, time left, reveal % so the auction loop is legible
Introduce a focal/active lot with elevation and detail panel instead of six equal-weight cards
Develop a typographic system (serif display + small caps labels) to carry the nostalgic, archival tone
Specify reveal motion—grain dissolve, emulsion fade—to make the 'gradual reveal' tangible
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective concept and visceral mood are decent, but behavioral layer is severely underbuilt—nothing tells you how to bid or what's being revealed.
rationale.intent_fit: Captures the atmosphere of a memory auction but fails to operationalize bidding or progressive polaroid revelation, leaving the brief half-answered.
